subject: Follow-up: Competitive eval & per-1M token TCO (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena.gutierrez@acme-retail.com>, Samir Rao <samir@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Competitive eval & per-1M token TCO (Acme Retail)

Hi Elena / Samir—

Great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the competitive items you asked us to surface. TL;DR below, followed by the assumptions we used for the per-1M token numbers.

TL;DR
- Redwood shows a ~30–45% lower per-1M-token unit cost vs the hyperscaler-managed endpoints for your summary workload when using batching (avg batch=8) and prefix KV caching (anticipated 40% hit rate).
- Key differentiators: integrated KV/prefix caching, automatic batching tuned per-route, and predictable Dedicated capacity (SLA-backed) versus bursty hyperscaler pricing.
- Proposed next test: 48-hour POC on a subset (search + rerank + dialog generation) with your dev cluster keys; we’ll instrument token-level cost and latency and deliver a TCO report.

Assumptions & unit economics (per-1M input+output tokens):
- Workload profile: 70% generation (avg 256 tokens output), 30% embeddings/rerank.
- Baseline hyperparameter assumptions: avg sequence length 320 tokens, concurrency 150 req/s during peak.

Estimated costs (ballpark, for comparison):
1) Redwood (hosted, mixed model + batching + 40% cache hit)
   - Model runtime + infra: $210 per 1M tokens
   - Caching savings: -$60 (40% effective)
   - Network & misc: $15
   - Net: ~$165 / 1M tokens

2) Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (typical GPU-backed endpoint + per-request overhead)
   - Model runtime + infra: $320 per 1M tokens
   - No effective prefix caching by default: $0
   - Network & misc: $25
   - Net: ~$345 / 1M tokens

3) Public LLM API (batching limited, higher per-token rate)
   - List rate: ~$400 per 1M tokens (no batching or KV cache)

Notes on assumptions:
- Batching: numbers assume we achieve an average batch size of 8 for generation paths. Batching reduces GPU utilization inefficiency but can increase tail latency for single-turn interactive flows. We can tune per-route scheduling to balance cost vs p95 latency.
- Caching: 40% hit rate is conservative for your e-commerce search rerank flow (many repeated prefixes for product/faq queries). If your actual hit rate is >60%, Redwood TCO improves materially.
- Headroom: Dedicated reserved pools and autoscaling reduce spot price variance and make monthly TCO predictable for steady sustained throughput.

Attachments: I attached a short worksheet that breaks the per-1M token math and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP).

Next steps I propose:
1) Approve a 48-hour POC scope (we’ll provide test harness + telemetry).
2) Schedule a 30-min tech sync with your infra/ML infra lead to agree on keys, network, and sample dataset (suggested window: next Wed/Thu).
3) We’ll run baseline tests (Redwood vs one hyperscaler endpoint) and deliver a comparative TCO report + latency profiles.

If that sounds good I’ll loop in Lauren to coordinate technical setup and Evelyn for commercial/commit details.

Thanks again—
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Elena Gutierrez <elena.gutierrez@acme-retail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & per-1M token TCO (Acme Retail)

Hi Marcus—

Thanks for the clear summary and the worksheet. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock the POC scope:

1) The numbers above look promising. For comparison, we're also testing Hyperscaler-A and Public-API-B. Can you confirm the model family you used for Redwood's estimate (e.g., rwd-3.1-llama or rwd-4.0-rl)? Also, what quantization level/instance footprint did you assume?

2) On caching: when you say prefix/KV caching at 40% hit rate, is that primarily for rerank/search or do you expect benefit on conversational dialog (we have a lot of short, repeated intents)?

3) For the POC telemetry, can we require token-level cost attribution and row-level traceability (per request id) so our finance and infra teams can reconcile billings?

If you can answer quickly we’ll aim to sign-off and get our infra lead (Samir) added to the tech sync.

Cheers,
Elena
VP Product | Acme Retail
elena.gutierrez@acme-retail.com

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena.gutierrez@acme-retail.com>, Samir Rao <samir@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-23T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & per-1M token TCO (Acme Retail)

Elena—

Answers inline: 

1) Model & infra assumptions: We used rwd-3.1-family (high-throughput variant) for generation estimates and a smaller ranking model (rwd-embed-1-small) for rerank/embeddings. Execution assumed int8 quantization for rwd-3.1 and an instance fleet equivalent to Dedicated m10-sized GPU pools for peak concurrency. If you prefer rwd-4.0-rl for qualitative parity with Hyperscaler-A, we can re-run the worksheet (estimate will increase ~15–25% on runtime but caching/ batching assumptions still apply).

2) Caching: The 40% hit rate primarily comes from search/rerank (product queries and category-level repeats). For conversation, short repeated intents will also benefit but typically at a lower hit-rate (~15–25%) unless you have persistent session prefixes we can cache. We can instrument the POC to measure per-route hit rates and report them back.

3) Telemetry: Yes — we can provide token-level cost attribution and per-request trace IDs. Our telemetry export includes request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, cache_hit boolean, and per-request cost attribution. We’ll include a CSV export you can reconcile with finance.

Next steps: Lauren, can you propose two technical windows for the sync (30 mins) and a short POC runbook? Evelyn, I’ll need a commercial review for the MAP (term sheet + trial credits).

Thanks—
Marcus

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena.gutierrez@acme-retail.com>, Samir Rao <samir@acme-retail.com>

Hi Elena / Samir—

Thanks for the questions — here are two windows that work for us to do the 30-min tech sync:
- Wednesday 2026-03-10 09:00–09:30 PT
- Thursday 2026-03-11 13:00–13:30 PT

POC runbook (short):
1) Access: You’ll provide a short sample dataset (anonymized) and a service account key we’ll use from our side for the 48-hour run.
2) Baseline: Run 6-hour baseline on your Hyperscaler-A endpoint and Redwood hosted endpoint with identical inputs.
3) Instrumentation: We’ll enable token-level telemetry and export CSV with request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit, batch_size, latency_p50/p95, and cost attribution.
4) Analysis: Redwood will deliver a TCO summary (per-1M tokens) and a latency/percentile profile plus a short recommendations doc (batching/cache tuning).

We’ll attach a brief checklist and the MAP for signature in the invite once Marcus confirms commercial terms.

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
